contributions.statement: If agents compose an existing pipeline through an MCP registry of operators, also ship procedural skill docs for the non-obvious composition steps, because registry access alone dropped pass rate to 83.3% vs 93.3% with skills, with the gain concentrated on 3 procedurally complex tasks.
contributions.evidence: Table 1 and Table 3: 12 tasks x 10 runs, Claude Opus 4.7 only; 1a/1b/3b go 18/30 to 29/30 with skills; authors' own benchmark.

contributions.statement: Let agents change a pipeline only through typed mutations that are committed after acyclicity and adjacent-schema compatibility checks.
contributions.evidence: §3 design and Table 1 cost reduction (72.5% vs vanilla); validation's contribution is not isolated by ablation and the action space differs from baselines; structurally valid DAGs still failed semantically on tasks 4a/4b.

reason: The MCP-only vs MCP-plus-skills comparison with repeated runs gives a measured boundary for when a registry API is not enough; the validated-mutation design is plausible but unablated.
